'''Valentine Louis "Val" Telegdi''' ([[Hungarian language|Hungarian]]: ''Telegdi Bálint''; 11 January 1922 &ndash; April 8, 2006) was a [[Kingdom of Hungary (1920–46)|Hungarian]]-American [[physicist]].

== Biography==
Valentine Telegdi was born in 1922 in Budapest, Hungary, in a [[Jewish]] family. His father, Georges, was from Pécs, Hungary, while his mother, Ella Csillag, was from Békéscsaba. His father studied commerce in Budapest, and went to Paris after graduation. He was detained as an enemy alien during the war, and returned to Budapest after five years. Several years later, finding the life in Hungary under [[Bela Kun]] to be difficult, he found a job for a transportation company in Bulgaria. His mother returned to Budapest to give birth. Valentine spent his early childhood in Bulgaria and Romania, and returned to Hungary in 1928. In 1932, the family moved to Vienna. Val was interested in science, and at 13 received a chemistry set as a gift. After a minor incident his parents forbade chemistry experiments at home. In Vienna, Telegdi studied at the ''Lehr- und Versuchsanstalt für chemische Industrie'', which trained laboratory technicians. Telegdi was left in Vienna to live with boarding families when his parents moved to Italy. He was in Milan on vacation in 1938, when the [[Anschluss]] of Austria happened.<ref name=rsbm>{{Cite journal | last1 = Brown | first1 = Laurie M. | doi = 10.1098/rsbm.2009.0012 | publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London|title = Valentine Louis Telegdi. 11 January 1922 - 8 April 2006 | journal = [[Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society]] | volume = 55 | pages = 291–304 | year = 2009 | doi-access = free }}</ref>

Telegdi continued his education at Bergamo and then Brussels. Belgium was occupied when he studied there, but as a Hungarian citizen he was able to leave the country for Italy. His father left for Switzerland, but Val with his mother stayed in Italy. There, he first earned a living doing technical translations, and later started to work at a patent office. He had a good salary, and, at 21 years old, his own secretary. In 1943, he and his mother illegally crossed Swiss border, and after a short internment joined Georges in Lausanne.<ref name=rsbm/>

Telegdi enrolled to the [[University of Lausanne]] and got a degree in chemical engineering and physical chemistry. He became interested in physics, and with the help from [[Ernst Stueckelberg]] was admitted to [[ETH Zurich]] in 1946. He started to work with [[Paul Scherrer]], and  later with [[Wolfgang Pauli]]. Both Scherrer and Pauli became his thesis supervisors.<ref name=rsbm/>

[[Victor Weisskopf]] recommended Telegdi to [[Enrico Fermi]], and he joined the [[University of Chicago]] in 1951. There Telegdi made major contributions to understanding weak interactions and symmetry violations. His 1957 experiment with [[Jerome Isaac Friedman|Jerome Friedman]] using nuclear emulsions independently confirmed parity non-conservation, though a controversial publication delay caused lasting frustration. He became so identified with muon research—studying muon capture, muonium properties, and the muon's magnetic moment—that colleagues called him "Mr. Muon". With [[Valentine Bargmann]] and [[Louis Michel]], he developed the [[BMT equation]] for relativistic spin precession. In 1972, Chicago named him the first Enrico Fermi Distinguished Service Professor.<ref name=rsbm/><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Ericson|first1=Torleif|last2=Freudenreich|first2=Klaus|last3=Martin|first3=André|title=Valentine L Tegledi 1922-2006|journal=CERN Courier|date=September 2006|volume=46|issue=7|page=49|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1733962}}</ref>

[[File:Val Telegdi christmas (cropped).png|thumb|Val Telegdi with cats, December 1965]]

Telegdi left Chicago in 1976 for positions at ETH Zurich and CERN, where he later chaired the Scientific Policy Committee. He and his wife Lidia, whom he had met in Zurich in 1947, settled in Geneva. After retiring from ETH in 1981 he divided his time between [[CERN]] and the [[California Institute of Technology]].<ref name=rsbm/> Telegdi chaired CERN's scientific policy committee from 1981 to 1983.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chairs of the Scientific Policy Committee {{!}} CERN Council |url=https://council.web.cern.ch/en/content/chairs-scientific-policy-committee |access-date=2025-01-17 |website=council.web.cern.ch}}</ref><ref name=aip>{{Cite web|url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11610008.html|title=Telegdi, Val, 1922-2006|website=history.aip.org}}</ref> He was chair of the International Committee for Future Accelerators, a working group of the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics]], from 1983 to 1986.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Membership {{!}} ICFA |url=https://icfa.hep.net/membership/ |access-date=2025-01-17 |language=en-US}}</ref> 

According to [[György Marx]] he was one of [[The Martians (scientists)|The Martians]].<ref>[http://fizikaiszemle.hu/archivum/fsz9703/marsl.html A marslakók legendája] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220409175959/http://fizikaiszemle.hu/archivum/fsz9703/marsl.html |date=2022-04-09 }} - [[György Marx]]</ref> Telegdi was fluent in Hungarian, German, Italian, and English, but had strong accent only in English. Known for incisive criticism and demanding intellectual standards reminiscent of Wolfgang Pauli, Telegdi earned a reputation as a "conscience of physics". He died on 8 April 2006.<ref name=rsbm/>

==Awards and honours==
Telegdi was elected to the National Academy of Sciences in 1968.<ref name=rsbm/> In 1991 he shared the [[Wolf Prize in Physics]] with [[Maurice Goldhaber]] "for their separate seminal contributions to nuclear and particle physics, particularly those concerning the weak interactions involving leptons".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Valentine L. Telegdi |url=https://wolffund.org.il/valentine-l-telegdi/ |access-date=2025-01-17 |website=Wolf Foundation |language=en-US}}</ref> He was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2003|Foreign Member of the Royal Society (ForMemRS) in 2003]].<ref name=rsbm/><ref>{{cite journal|author=[[Nicola Cabibbo|Cabibbo, Nicola]]; [[Peter Freund|Freund, Peter G. O.]]; [[Murray Gell-Mann|Gell-Mann, Murray]]; [[Marvin Leonard Goldberger|Goldberger, Marvin L.]]; [[Yoichiro Nambu|Nambu, Yoichiro]]; [[Reinhard Oehme|Oehme, Reinhard]]; [[Lev Okun|Okun, Lev]]; [[Roland Winston|Winston, Roland]]|title=Obituary: Valentine Louis Telegdi|journal=Physics Today|date=July 2006|volume=59|issue=7|pages=66–67|doi=10.1063/1.2337842|bibcode=2006PhT....59g..66C|url=https://authors.library.caltech.edu/59846/|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Royal Society elections recognize research in particles and waves|journal=CERN Courier|date=October 2003|volume=43|issue=8|page=36|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1733534}}</ref>
